title: Audit ingest: sampled journalization and cost-governor for high-cardinality tenants
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: We need a robust ingestion strategy for audit events that reduces storage and query cost for extremely high-cardinality tenants while preserving forensic fidelity for security-sensitive events. The plan introduces sampled journalization (tiered sampling with guaranteed retention for high-severity events), compact partitioning heuristics, and a cost-governor that enforces tenant-level ingest rate caps with soft-failbacks to write-ahead cold storage. This ticket covers design, implementation, and rollout for the ingestion + storage side and how RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML audit hooks are prioritized and preserved across sampling.

Background: Several incidents and internal cost analysis showed a small set of tenants generate the majority of audit volume (auth attempts, token churn, session telemetry). Storing all events at full fidelity leads to prohibitively high hot-store costs and degraded query performance for tenant-scoped forensic queries. Existing tickets focus on index compaction and TTL policies, but we need an upstream approach to reduce hot ingest pressure and make cost controls tenant-aware and security-aware.

Goals: 
- Reduce hot-store tokenized storage cost by 40% for top 5% busiest tenants without losing ability to investigate critical security incidents.
- Ensure high-severity events (SSO failures, RBAC change events, admin API calls) are always retained at full fidelity for at least 90 days.
- Provide per-tenant and per-customer cost-governor metrics surfaced in Console (usage + throttle events).
- Integrate with RBAC v2: preserve actor and permission-change context for sampled events so audit trails remain useful.

Scope: ingest pipeline (front-end tier + write-ahead journal), sampling policy engine, storage partitioning policy, coldstore journaling for sampled-upgraded retrieval, and Console telemetry. Does NOT include UI changes to billing pages (follow-up ticket).

Design proposal: 
1) Sampled journalization: For each tenant, ingest flow writes to an append-only journal for immediate durability. A sampling evaluator consumes the journal and decides per-event retention class: FULL, INDEXED_ONLY, SUMMARY, DROP. Sampling rules: 
   - Events with severity in {ERROR, SECURITY, RBAC_CHANGE, SAML_FAILURE} => FULL.
   - Session start/heartbeat events sampled at 1% by default but upsample on detection of anomaly heuristics.
   - Tenant-level adaptive sampler: maintains sliding-window ingest rate and reduces sampling as rate increases, subject to a settable floor for critical event retention.
2) Cost-governor: A per-tenant enforcement module that: 
   - Exposes soft and hard thresholds (soft triggers alerts and increases sampling aggressiveness; hard rejects non-critical events or routes them to coldstore).
   - Records governor decisions as audit meta-events (so operator actions are visible).
3) Partitioning & indexing heuristics: 
   - Compact partitions by time + tenant + severity class. Low-severity sampled events land in denser compressed shards with low retention. Full events go to hot shards with KV index.
   - Provide a lightweight per-tenant summary index to support the most common queries (actor list, change sequences) without rehydrating full blobs.
4) Coldstore rehydration path: 
   - Sampled or dropped events are retained in cost-optimized coldstore for 365 days by default. Rehydration API lets SREs or Compliance request full replays for incident windows, and an automated path rehydrates events when a security incident flag is raised.

Alternatives considered: 
- Aggressive TTL only: too destructive for forensic needs.
- Full deduplication at ingest: complex and expensive CPU cost for stream dedupe.
- Tenant-level rate limiting without sampling: causes more dropped critical events.

Trade-offs and decisions: 
- Keeping a write-ahead journal increases storage briefly but ensures we can make sampling decisions asynchronously without increasing request latency. Decision: accept extra transient storage use.
- Guaranteeing full retention for RBAC/SAML events increases hot-store cost slightly; we accept this for compliance.
- Rehydration latency is accepted up to minutes for incidents; not intended for real-time UI queries.

Implementation plan: 
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement sampled journalization consumer, base sampling rules, cost-governor prototype, and partition metadata changes. Add telemetry for governor events. (Owners: Liam Chen, Priya Rao)
- Phase 2: integrate RBAC v2 event classification and SAML hook enrichment, extend Console metrics and alerting, add coldstore rehydration API.
- Phase 3: load test and tune sampling parameters, rollout to canary tenants, then gradual ramp.

Acceptance criteria: 
- End-to-end pipeline can classify and route events into FULL/INDEXED_ONLY/SUMMARY/DROP and maintain an append-only journal for 72 hours.
- Sampling rules preserved RBAC and SAML events at 100% fidelity.
- Cost-governor metrics appear in Console telemetry for canary tenants.
- Load tests show 35-50% reduction in hot-store writes for targeted tenants under realistic traffic.

Monitoring and alerts: 
- Alerts on governor hard-throttle events > 0.1% of tenant traffic.
- Dashboards: ingest rate by tenant, sampling ratio by severity, coldstore rehydrate queue length, rehydration job success/failure.

Security & compliance notes: 
- Security review required (string flag set). RBAC metadata must be computed before sampling decision, to avoid losing actor context.
- All journals encrypted at-rest using KMS; rehydration access gated by RBAC v2 admin controls.

Open questions: 
- Should the default coldstore retention be 365 or 730 days for regulated customers? (Need compliance input).
- What SLA will we commit to for rehydration latency?
- Should we expose per-tenant sampling knobs in the Console or keep control with SRE only?

Links and artifacts: 
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Sampled+Journalization+Design (draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1289
- Load test plan and results: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ingest-load-tests/2026-03
- Incident notes referencing high-cardinality tenant: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-02-Auth-Spike

Stakeholder reviews: 
- Security review requested with SecEng (requested 2026-03-05).
- PM feedback: prefer conservative defaults; provide per-tenant override via support.
- Design review: request design review with DesignOps for Console telemetry UX after Phase 1.

Next steps: 
- Implement consumer and cost-governor prototype and open preliminary PR.
- Run ingestion load test with synthetic high-cardinality tenant and collect metrics.
- Schedule security review meeting and finalize retention policy for regulated customers.
implementation_steps: Add write-ahead journal to ingest front-end with KMS encryption
Build sampling-evaluator service that consumes journal and emits routing decisions
Implement cost-governor library with soft/hard thresholds and telemetry hooks
Adjust partition assignment to include severity-class and tenant bucketing
Add coldstore writer for sampled/dropped events with rehydration index
Instrument Console with sampling and governor metrics for canary tenants
Write integration tests and run load tests using canary dataset
